requirements.title: Dual User Interface Support
requirements.description: The Model Manager system shall be accessible to users through both a web-based GUI and a command line tool.

source_references.excerpt: The MM will be accessible from a web-based GUI and a command line tool.

requirements.title: Centralized Multi-Cluster Node Allocation
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall manage jobs across one or more clusters and provide centralized control and node allocation.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: The MM will manage jobs on one or more clusters.

requirements.title: Automated Setup of Real-Time and Off-Line Weather FDDA Jobs
requirements.description: The Job-Setup module shall allow users to set up and schedule real-time and off-line Weather FDDA model jobs.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to automate the set up of new real time and off-line FDDA jobs.

requirements.title: ClimoFDDA Job Setup and Functional Integration
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall integrate GCAT functionalities to allow users to set up, configure, and schedule ClimoFDDA model jobs.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to integrate the GCAT functionalities within the MM.

requirements.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job Submission
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall provide the capability to set up and execute post-processing jobs independently on existing model output files.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to only run “post-processing” on an existing model output file.

requirements.title: By-Hand Custom Job Registration
requirements.description: Users shall be able to register existing 'by-hand' custom jobs with the Model Manager by supplying mandatory execution parameters.

source_references.excerpt: In order for the MM to accept the job, the user will have to provide certain mandatory information about the job.

requirements.title: Job Configuration Loading and File Re-submission
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall allow users to load job configurations from a saved file, edit them, and submit the resulting job.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to load a job configuration into MM from a file.

requirements.title: Retrieval and Editing of Previously Saved Job Configurations
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall allow logged-in users to retrieve, modify, save, or re-run previously saved job configurations.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to retrieve a previous job configuration and to re-run this job or change its settings and run it again.

requirements.title: Job Queue and Status Monitoring
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall present job tables displaying scheduled, running, and historical jobs along with detailed attributes and status.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to facilitate monitoring of running jobs, viewing the job queue and viewing jobs that ran in the past.

requirements.title: Job Control and Privileged Deletion/Stop/Restart Actions
requirements.description: Users shall be able to stop, restart, resume, or delete their own jobs, while super users can execute these actions on any job.

source_references.excerpt: A “super user” can delete any job from the job queue.

requirements.title: MetVault Integration Independence
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall operate seamlessly either in conjunction with MetVault or as a stand-alone application with no MetVault dependency.

source_references.excerpt: The MM can run in conjunction with the MetVault, and it can also run as a stand-alone application with no knowledge about a MetVault.

requirements.title: Automation of Model Job Setup and Execution
requirements.description: The Model Manager shall automate the setup, execution, and monitoring of model jobs to improve efficiency across NSAP operations.

source_references.excerpt: The primary goal of this project is to extend the current model back end system and to automate the setup, running and monitoring of model jobs.

scenarios.title: Successful Web-based GUI Job Setup Access
scenarios.objective: Verify that a user can access job setup features using the web-based GUI interface.
preconditions: User is connected to the network and has web browser access.

source_references.excerpt: The MM will be accessible from a web-based GUI and a command line tool.

scenarios.title: Automatic Cluster Selection for New Job
scenarios.objective: Verify that the Model Manager automatically selects appropriate cluster resources when the user does not specify a cluster.
preconditions: Multiple clusters managed by the Model Manager are operational.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: S/he will submit a job to the MM and the MM will make the decision on what cluster(s) the job will be running.

scenarios.title: Weather FDDA Job Setup with Historical Time Prompt
scenarios.objective: Verify that specifying a past cycle time prompts the user to classify the job as a case study or re-run.
preconditions: User is configuring a Weather FDDA job in the Job-Setup module.

source_references.excerpt: If the cycle time is in the past, then the user is prompted to specify whether the job is a “case study” or “re-run”.

scenarios.title: ClimoFDDA Job Setup and Submission
scenarios.objective: Verify complete creation and submission of a ClimoFDDA job with domain and timeline settings.
preconditions: User is logged on and selecting Climo job setup.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to integrate the GCAT functionalities within the MM.

scenarios.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job Submission for Existing File
scenarios.objective: Verify creation and execution of a standalone post-processing job using an existing model output file.
preconditions: Model output file exists on accessible storage.

source_references.excerpt: If the model output file already exists, then the user supplies its location.

scenarios.title: By-Hand Job Registration Validation
scenarios.objective: Verify registration of a custom by-hand job when all required mandatory fields are provided.
preconditions: Custom script exists on target cluster.

source_references.excerpt: In order for the MM to accept the job, the user will have to provide certain mandatory information about the job.

scenarios.title: Load and Re-submit Job Configuration File
scenarios.objective: Verify loading an existing configuration file, editing parameters, and submitting the job.
preconditions: A valid job configuration file is available on disk.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to load a job configuration into MM from a file.

scenarios.title: Retrieve and Re-run Previously Saved Job Configuration
scenarios.objective: Verify retrieving a saved job from the saved configurations table and resubmitting it after updates.
preconditions: User has previously saved at least one job configuration in the system.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to retrieve a previous job configuration and to re-run this job or change its settings and run it again.

scenarios.title: View Job Queue and Detailed Job Attributes
scenarios.objective: Verify filtering and viewing running, scheduled, and past jobs in the job table.
preconditions: Multiple jobs exist in various states (scheduled, running, old).

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: User chooses to look at all running jobs, all scheduled jobs (the job queue), past jobs or all jobs (running, scheduled, old).

scenarios.title: Super User Deletes Job Owned by Another User
scenarios.objective: Verify that a super user can delete any job from the queue while standard users cannot delete others' jobs.
preconditions: A job owned by regular User A exists in the job queue.

source_references.excerpt: A “super user” can delete any job from the job queue.

scenarios.title: Job Setup and Execution Without MetVault Integration
scenarios.objective: Verify that job setup and execution function properly in standalone mode without MetVault present.
preconditions: Model Manager instance is deployed in standalone mode with no MetVault connection.

source_references.excerpt: The MM can run in conjunction with the MetVault, and it can also run as a stand-alone application with no knowledge about a MetVault.

test_cases.title: Access Job Setup via Web GUI
preconditions: Web interface service is active.

steps.action: Open web browser and navigate to Model Manager web application URL.
steps.expected_result: Model Manager login/main dashboard loads successfully.

steps.action: Log in with valid user credentials.
steps.expected_result: User is presented with core options: Submit a new job, Retrieve saved job configurations, and View job queue.

steps.action: Click 'Submit a new job' and select 'Set up a new model job'.
steps.expected_result: Job-Setup options 'Weather FDDA' and 'Climo' are displayed.

source_references.excerpt: The MM will be accessible from a web-based GUI and a command line tool.

test_cases.title: Automatic Cluster Allocation on Job Submission
preconditions: At least two clusters are connected and healthy.

steps.action: Initiate new Weather FDDA job setup and leave cluster selection blank.
steps.expected_result: System allows user to proceed without specifying cluster.

steps.action: Complete required job parameters (JOBID, model WRF, domain) and click Submit.
steps.expected_result: Job is submitted successfully.

steps.action: Check job details in job queue.
steps.expected_result: Model Manager has automatically assigned an active target cluster to the running job.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: S/he will submit a job to the MM and the MM will make the decision on what cluster(s) the job will be running.

test_cases.title: Historical Cycle Time Triggers Re-run Prompt
preconditions: Job-Setup module open.

steps.action: Start Weather FDDA job configuration and assign JOBID 'HIST_TEST_01'.
steps.expected_result: JOBID is accepted.

steps.action: Enter a historical cycle time that is prior to current time.
steps.expected_result: System prompts user to specify whether job is 'case study' or 're-run'.

steps.action: Select 're-run' and complete submission.
steps.expected_result: Job is classified and submitted as an off-line FDDA re-run job.

source_references.excerpt: If the cycle time is in the past, then the user is prompted to specify whether the job is a “case study” or “re-run”.

test_cases.title: Configure and Submit ClimoFDDA Job
preconditions: Logged in with valid scientist role.

steps.action: Select 'Set up a Climo Job' and enter JOBID 'CLIMO_JOB_01'.
steps.expected_result: Climo configuration panel opens.

steps.action: Set domain location, pick pre-configured MM5 setup, and define start time, end time, and years timeline.
steps.expected_result: Parameters are accepted.

steps.action: Configure ensemble options (hourly, min, max, mean) and submit job.
steps.expected_result: ClimoFDDA job is registered and added to schedule.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to integrate the GCAT functionalities within the MM.

test_cases.title: Standalone Post-Processing on Existing Output File
preconditions: Input file available at specified path.

steps.action: Select 'Set up a new post-processing job'.
steps.expected_result: Post-processing setup page is displayed.

steps.action: Supply file location for existing model output file '/data/output/model_run.nc'.
steps.expected_result: File path is validated.

steps.action: Choose post-processing type 'Plots (NCL or RIP)', specify destination host/location, and submit.
steps.expected_result: Post-processing job executes and generates plots at destination.

source_references.excerpt: If the model output file already exists, then the user supplies its location.

test_cases.title: Register Custom By-Hand Job with Mandatory Information
preconditions: Script is staged on target cluster host.

steps.action: Select 'Submit a By Hand Job'.
steps.expected_result: By-hand registration form opens.

steps.action: Enter mandatory details: job id 'GWDPG', script location 'cluster1:/scripts/run.sh', run time, estimated duration, executable names, max runtime, and output location.
steps.expected_result: Form fields pass validation.

steps.action: Submit the job and open job queue.
steps.expected_result: Custom job 'GWDPG' appears in job queue.

source_references.excerpt: In order for the MM to accept the job, the user will have to provide certain mandatory information about the job.

test_cases.title: Load, Modify, and Submit Job Configuration File
preconditions: Valid configuration file exists.

steps.action: Select 'Submit a job configuration file'.
steps.expected_result: File selection prompt appears.

steps.action: Supply configuration file name 'saved_config.json' and load contents.
steps.expected_result: Configuration values populate the setup editor.

steps.action: Modify forecast length parameter, save changes, and submit job.
steps.expected_result: Updated configuration is submitted and job enters queue.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to load a job configuration into MM from a file.

test_cases.title: Retrieve, Edit, and Re-run Saved Job Configuration
preconditions: At least one saved job exists.

steps.action: Navigate to saved job configurations table.
steps.expected_result: List of user's previously saved jobs is shown.

steps.action: Select job 'JOB_SAVED_01' and click change.
steps.expected_result: Job parameters are opened for editing.

steps.action: Update cycle interval parameter, save changed job configuration, and click submit.
steps.expected_result: Modified job configuration is saved and job executes.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to retrieve a previous job configuration and to re-run this job or change its settings and run it again.

test_cases.title: View and Filter Job Monitoring Table
preconditions: System has active and historical jobs recorded.

steps.action: Navigate to job monitoring interface and select view 'all jobs'.
steps.expected_result: Job table displays running, scheduled, and past jobs.

steps.action: Verify displayed table columns.
steps.expected_result: Columns for user id, job id, job type, priority, start time, remaining time, cycle, stage, status, cluster/nodes, and processors are visible.

steps.action: Select a running job row to request detailed info.
steps.expected_result: Detailed information and link to job log files are displayed.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to facilitate monitoring of running jobs, viewing the job queue and viewing jobs that ran in the past.

test_cases.title: Super User Deletes Job Belonging to Another User
preconditions: Job 'USERA_JOB_99' exists in job queue.

steps.action: Log in as super user account.
steps.expected_result: Super user administrative dashboard is active.

steps.action: Locate job 'USERA_JOB_99' owned by standard user 'UserA' in job queue.
steps.expected_result: Job is identified in SCHEDULED state.

steps.action: Execute delete command on 'USERA_JOB_99'.
steps.expected_result: Job is successfully deleted from the queue.

source_references.excerpt: A “super user” can delete any job from the job queue.

test_cases.title: Standalone Operation Without MetVault
preconditions: MetVault service is completely absent/unreachable.

steps.action: Start Model Manager instance configured in standalone mode without MetVault endpoints.
steps.expected_result: Model Manager initializes without errors or missing dependency alerts.

steps.action: Configure and submit a model job giving local directory inputs instead of MetVault sources.
steps.expected_result: Job setup succeeds and job is queued.

steps.action: Monitor execution to completion.
steps.expected_result: Job runs to completion and outputs are saved to local filesystem.

source_references.excerpt: The MM can run in conjunction with the MetVault, and it can also run as a stand-alone application with no knowledge about a MetVault.
